literal: Learned ones before, learned things to reach having spoken, oneself learned things, those who are greater among, greater things taking.
translation: Speak what you have learned convincingly before the learned; and from those who are more learned, grasp what is greater than your own learning.
modern: கற்றறிந்த அறிஞர்கள் முன்னே தான் கற்றவற்றை அவர்கள் மனத்தில் பதியுமாறு தெளிவாகச் சொல்ல வேண்டும். அதே சமயம், தன்னை விட அதிகமாகக் கற்ற அறிஞர்களிடமிருந்து தான் கற்றதை விட மேலான கருத்துகளைக் கேட்டு அறிந்துகொள்ள வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the dual responsibility of a learned person in an assembly. First, one must articulate their own knowledge clearly and convincingly before other scholars. Second, one must remain humble and receptive, actively acquiring deeper knowledge from those who are more learned. The word 'செல' (to go/reach) emphasizes that speaking is not just uttering words, but ensuring the ideas successfully reach and convince the audience's minds.
